title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 305: The Chill of History: The Little Ice Age
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 305 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Chill of History: Navigating the Little Ice Age

Paragraph 1. Between about 1300 and 1850, the Earth went through a long cool period called the Little Ice Age. World temperatures only dropped by about one degree Celsius, so it was not a true giant ice age. Even so, this small change caused huge trouble across Europe, Asia, and North America. Big mountain glaciers grew larger and destroyed Swiss villages, and the River Thames in London froze so hard that people held winter fairs on the ice.

Paragraph 2. For many years, history books said wars and falling kingdoms in the 1600s happened only because of bad kings and heavy taxes. Now, climate scientist Dr. Raymond Douglas offers another answer. He studied old polar ice, tree rings, and farm records. His research shows that cold weather made existing political problems much worse and pushed weak countries toward disaster.

Paragraph 3. Cold weather hurt farming first. In the 1600s, the growing season became up to four weeks shorter. Cold, wet weather in spring rotted seeds in the ground, and early frosts in autumn killed crops. Food prices jumped high, and millions of hungry people became too weak to fight off terrible sicknesses.

Paragraph 4. However, not every country broke down in the cold. Unfair kingdoms like Russia faced violent riots when harvests failed. In contrast, the Dutch Republic stayed strong and rich. The Dutch bought grain from other lands by ship and even used frozen rivers like highways for skates and winter sleds.
